learningObjective: Capture one coherent provider configuration per stream while later streams receive a published replacement.

question.prompt: In a live captioning studio, the caption supervisor must switch the active language provider. The current stream keeps its timing and error contract. Each open stream captures both provider and timing settings at start; new streams use the latest published pair. What should provider switching publish?

options.text: Start a different stream identity for each provider change even when the same stream continues.
Choose immutable config snapshots for each stream’s captured provider/timing pair, with a replacement active config for future streams.
Change the provider field on the shared configuration while streams are active.
Cache a stream’s timing value but resolve its provider from the latest global configuration on every frame.
Keep both old and new settings in one mutable object and ask each stream to coordinate which fields it reads.

feedback.reason: The stream’s capture point applies to the whole provider-and-timing configuration. Resolving one field live would combine values from different configuration versions.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A consumer-specific immutable snapshot lets an ongoing stream keep the values it captured while a published replacement serves later streams.
details.scenarioApplication: The stream’s timing and provider form one captured configuration; publication affects new streams while existing streams keep their original pair.
details.errorCorrection: Resolving the provider live but retaining old timing would combine two versions within one stream; the prompt captures both together.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The per-stream capture point is the boundary; immediate switching of an already open stream would require a different explicit contract.
details.transfer: For long-lived consumers, state which version they capture and which publication serves new consumers.

messages.text: That changes a value already captured by an open stream.
The provider would be live while timing remains captured, mixing configuration versions.
Callers cannot coordinate a coherent pair if both settings can change separately.
A provider switch does not end the stream under the stated continuity contract.

learningObjective: Copy a mutable nested assignment graph so editing a draft cannot alter a submitted proposal.

question.prompt: In a volunteer coordination hub, the shift manager must swap two volunteer assignments. Skills and availability constraints hold for both assignments. The assignment list and each nested availability note are mutable. The submitted proposal must remain exactly reviewable while a separate draft is edited. How should the editor create the draft?

options.text: Freeze the submitted proposal and also forbid changes to an unsubmitted draft.
Let draft screens edit the submitted notes, then reconstruct the old text from audit timestamps.
Convert each volunteer into a new volunteer record whenever a note is corrected.
Copy the assignment graph, including each mutable note, into a separate draft; leave the submitted proposal unchanged.
Copy only the assignment list and edit the same note objects from the draft.

feedback.reason: A shallow list copy still points to the same mutable note objects, so editing the draft can alter the submitted proposal.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A copied collection is independent only when mutable objects reachable through it are no longer shared with the submitted proposal.
details.scenarioApplication: The mutable notes are reachable from both lists unless copied or converted to immutable values; the prompt requires the submitted text to remain reviewable.
details.errorCorrection: The draft’s notes would still be the same mutable objects as the submitted proposal, so a correction could rewrite what reviewers saw.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Drafts may remain editable; only the submitted proposal and its reachable mutable notes must be isolated.
details.transfer: When copying a graph, inspect whether nested values can still be mutated through a shared reference.

messages.text: The shared note is still mutable through the draft alias.
The scenario allows draft edits and only freezes submitted content.
Reconstructing history does not preserve the exact submitted text as a stable value.
The volunteer identity is unchanged by correcting an assignment note.

learningObjective: Keep an accepted route revision as a conflict baseline while editing a separate pending value.

question.prompt: In a local-first map editor, the cartographer must merge an offline route edit. Conflicts are explicit and never silently overwrite accepted geometry. Accepted geometry is retained as a conflict baseline; cartographers may edit only a pending revision before acceptance. How should a route correction be represented?

options.text: Create a separate pending route revision; retain accepted geometry as the baseline until the pending revision is accepted.
Apply pending points directly to the accepted geometry and label the result pending.
Copy the route wrapper but reuse the same mutable point list for the accepted and pending revisions.
Make the pending revision impossible to edit after its first save, even though it is still under review.
Give the route a new route identity for each edit although the prompt calls it another revision.

feedback.reason: The accepted geometry is the conflict baseline; mutating it before acceptance removes the comparison state the review needs.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Separate pending and accepted values preserve the accepted revision as a stable comparison baseline.
details.scenarioApplication: The key boundary is accepted versus pending revision; this does not require the pending draft itself to be immutable while it is being edited.
details.errorCorrection: The alternative overwrites the exact accepted geometry needed as the conflict baseline.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This freezes accepted geometry, not the pending draft before acceptance.
details.transfer: When review depends on a prior accepted value, keep the editable candidate separate until the defined acceptance point.

messages.text: This edits the baseline before the pending revision is accepted.
Both wrappers still reach the same mutable geometry.
The prompt permits an editable pending revision.
A route revision is not a new route identity here.

learningObjective: Capture the minimal immutable inputs for a transient calculation without turning it into permanent history.

question.prompt: In a board-game campaign manager, the campaign host must apply a reward to a character. Reward rules depend on the current legal campaign state. The preview is transient, not an audit record; its calculation must use one consistent set of character facts and the named rules revision. What should the calculation receive?

options.text: Capture only the character ID and let the calculation reread whichever rules are current later.
Create a new character identity for the preview so the input cannot change.
Use an ephemeral immutable calculation input; do not persist a permanent result snapshot for a preview that is discarded.
Reload the character and current rules separately during calculation so each field is fresh.
Persist a permanent historical copy of every character field and rules object even though the preview is discarded.

feedback.reason: The prompt requires a consistent input for this calculation, not permanent archival retention; a one-use immutable input value meets that contract.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Capture an immutable set of calculation inputs for this preview; its transient lifecycle does not require permanent archival copies.
details.scenarioApplication: This is an ephemeral calculation boundary: capture the inputs together for one preview, while reserving permanent provenance snapshots for published results.
details.errorCorrection: A permanent archive is unnecessary for a discarded preview, but rereading live inputs during its calculation would violate the one-input-set premise.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Discard the captured values after the preview; persistence is needed only if the result becomes a published record.
details.transfer: For transient calculations, capture the minimal input set together without accidentally turning it into permanent history.

messages.text: Separate live reads can mix character and rules from different moments.
The transient preview does not require permanent archival storage.
A current rules lookup is not the revision used in this calculation.
A preview does not create a new character.

learningObjective: Safely share an immutable child value while replacing the coupled plan that must be validated as a whole.

question.prompt: In a cold-chain logistics console, the dispatch planner must reassign a shipment to a carrier. Temperature restrictions and hand-off ownership travel with the shipment. The temperature-band value is immutable and may be shared; the approved plan is valid only when shipment, band, and custody handoff agree. How should a reassignment be prepared?

options.text: Validate temperature and custody separately, then publish without checking them together against the shipment as one approved plan.
Mutate the approved plan’s shipment first, then update temperature and custody separately.
Expose mutable plan fields so each dispatch client sequences the changes consistently.
Give the shipment a new identity when its carrier changes.
Replace the plan value while reusing its immutable temperature-band value; validate the new shipment and custody fields together.

feedback.reason: The temperature band is stated to be immutable, so sharing it cannot let one plan’s edit change another; the replacement still needs to validate the related fields together.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Immutable nested values can be shared safely, while the parent plan still needs a whole-value replacement for its coupled approval check.
details.scenarioApplication: The approval condition spans the shipment, its temperature band, and its custody handoff; the planner must validate that combined value before publication.
details.errorCorrection: The nearest wrong choice checks temperature and custody separately but never validates the combined plan against the shipment.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Share the immutable child but replace the mutable composite plan whose fields are validated together.
details.transfer: Share children only when their own contract makes them immutable; replace the parent that owns coupled changing values.

messages.text: Separate checks do not establish that the combined shipment, temperature band, and custody handoff form the approved plan.
This publishes part of a plan before its coupled approval check.
Caller ordering cannot replace the required whole-plan check.
Carrier reassignment does not change shipment identity.

learningObjective: Model a composite amount as a value whose currency and minor units both determine equivalence.

question.prompt: In a cooperative lending ledger, the account steward must record a repayment allocation. A repayment cannot reduce the outstanding balance below zero. Once posted, an allocation amount is fixed; a correction is a separate ledger entry. In this ledger, an amount is exactly (currency, minor units); 120 USD and 120 EUR differ, while equal pairs are interchangeable. How should an allocation represent its amount?

options.text: Store a formatted display string as the amount so parsing rules define equality.
Represent the allocation amount as an immutable value containing both currency and minor units.
Compare only the numeric minor-unit count and infer the currency from the account later.
Use a mutable amount object and update its currency after the allocation is posted.
Treat each amount as a separate identity even when both currency and minor units match.

feedback.reason: The prompt explicitly defines value equivalence using both currency and minor units; dropping currency makes a distinct amount compare as though it were the same value.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A composite value is equivalent only when all components named by the domain contract match.
details.scenarioApplication: This is value semantics for a composite amount, not entity identity: all stated components participate in the value.
details.errorCorrection: The numeric-only alternative ignores currency, which the prompt says is part of amount equivalence.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Use these equivalence components only because the prompt explicitly defines them; do not infer other amount rules.
details.transfer: For a value type, list every component that the domain says contributes to equivalence.

messages.text: Currency is explicitly part of amount equality.
The posted amount is an immutable value, not a mutable object to revise later.
The prompt defines equal component pairs as interchangeable values.
Formatting is not the stipulated currency-plus-units representation.

learningObjective: Represent a correction as a new immutable record linked to the finalized result it supersedes.

question.prompt: In a tournament bracket service, the match official must forfeit a match after a timeout. The bracket advances only from a legal match state. A correction must preserve the finalized result and identify which earlier result it supersedes. What should the official record?

options.text: Change the bracket’s live match object and rely on the audit screen to infer the prior winner.
Make the corrected result a mutable draft and let downstream rounds read it before approval.
Create a new tournament identity for the correction.
Append a correction record that points to the finalized result; retain the original result as an immutable historical fact.
Overwrite the finalized winner and keep the original result ID.

feedback.reason: The audit contract requires both the finalized result and the correction relationship; overwriting the original loses that distinction.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A correction record preserves the original immutable decision and names what it supersedes.
details.scenarioApplication: Immutable records work here because the domain needs a durable before/after trail, not merely a replaceable current value.
details.errorCorrection: Overwriting the result removes the earlier finalized fact that the correction must reference.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The original result and correction are distinct audit records; the prompt does not require a new tournament identity.
details.transfer: For corrections that must retain history, append a new immutable record linked to the earlier decision.

messages.text: This destroys the finalized result that the correction must supersede.
The prior value needs to remain explicitly available, not reconstructed from a changing screen.
Downstream readers must not consume a draft before approval.
The correction does not create a new tournament.

learningObjective: Freeze submitted condition facts while keeping a later eligibility decision in its own lifecycle.

question.prompt: In a returns inspection workflow, the warehouse inspector must classify a returned item. Classification and refund eligibility are not the same responsibility. The submitted condition category is an immutable report value; refund eligibility is calculated later from separate policy facts. What should submission do?

options.text: Submit an immutable condition-report value and keep the later refund decision outside that report.
Add a mutable refundEligible flag to the report and let inspection change it after submission.
Prevent inspectors from editing a draft before it is submitted.
Store only an item ID and recompute the submitted condition from the current inspection screen.
Give the returned physical item a new identity when its condition category is corrected.

feedback.reason: A refund result is not one of the submitted condition facts; storing it in the report conflates a stable observation with a later policy decision.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A submitted observation and a later policy outcome are different values with different lifecycles.
details.scenarioApplication: Freeze the report at submission, but do not mistake immutability for freezing the entire workflow or merging later decisions into it.
details.errorCorrection: A refund flag mixes a later policy result into the immutable inspection observation.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Freeze the condition report at submission; the later refund decision remains outside that snapshot.
details.transfer: Freeze observations at their submission point and keep later interpretation in its own contract.

messages.text: The refund decision is separate from the submitted condition observation.
Draft editing is allowed before submission.
Current screen state is not the submitted report.
The item identity survives a classification correction.

learningObjective: Retain exact immutable input-version references on a published computation for later audit.

question.prompt: In a research-notebook platform, the experiment owner must publish a result snapshot. Published outputs reference immutable inputs and code versions. A published run is retained for audit after current inputs change; it must point to the exact dataset and code revisions used. How should the published result retain provenance?

options.text: Allow the result’s provenance references to be edited when the experiment changes.
Give the experiment a new identity for each run instead of preserving run-level provenance.
Persist exact immutable dataset/code revision references on the audit-retained result; do not resolve “current” inputs later.
Resolve the experiment’s current dataset and code whenever the published result is opened.
Copy the dataset bytes but store “current” instead of the exact code revision used for the published run.

feedback.reason: A current-input pointer would make the published result refer to different inputs after the experiment changes; the prompt provides fixed revisions that can be retained.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A durable result can retain immutable revision references rather than resolving mutable current inputs.
details.scenarioApplication: This is durable provenance for a published computation, unlike a transient preview that only needs a consistent input during calculation.
details.errorCorrection: Copying dataset bytes does not satisfy provenance if the result stores only a moving “current” code reference.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The result needs both exact dataset and code revisions; the prompt does not require copying dataset bytes.
details.transfer: For durable reproducibility, keep exact input-version references with the published output.

messages.text: Current revisions can change and no longer identify the run inputs.
The run would lack its exact code revision, so later readers could not identify the code that produced it.
Editing provenance rewrites the published run’s meaning.
A run has its own provenance while the experiment remains the parent project.

learningObjective: Separate the immutable accepted comment from delivery state that changes during retries.

question.prompt: In a collaborative annotation workspace, the review editor must accept a comment and notify the assigned author. Accepted comments must retain their author and document revision. Accepted comment text, author, and document revision are fixed; notification delivery status changes as retries occur. How should the accepted comment and retry state relate?

options.text: Add each delivery attempt to the accepted comment so one object holds both immutable facts and changing retries.
Make the comment mutable until notification succeeds, then call it accepted.
Copy the text but read author and revision from the live editor whenever retry runs.
Create a new document revision for each notification attempt.
Keep accepted comment text, author, and revision in an immutable value; track retry status in a separate delivery record.

feedback.reason: A delivery retry does not change which text, author, or revision was accepted; mixing retry state into that tuple makes the accepted comment mutable.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An accepted value can be immutable while separate transport work continues changing.
details.scenarioApplication: Separate an accepted immutable value from the operational state that legitimately changes after acceptance.
details.errorCorrection: Putting retry state inside the accepted tuple changes the record the prompt says is fixed.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Delivery attempts can change independently without changing accepted comment facts.
details.transfer: Separate fixed accepted facts from operational state that changes after acceptance.

messages.text: Transport status can change without altering the accepted comment tuple.
Acceptance fixes the comment before delivery retries complete.
The accepted author and revision must not be read from mutable editor state.
A notification attempt does not create a document revision.

learningObjective: Retry the exact submitted payload rather than rebuilding it from a subsequently edited draft.

question.prompt: In a mobile field-inspection app, the inspector must submit an offline inspection. A submission is either complete or explicitly retryable. The server accepts only complete submissions. A retry must send the exact payload originally submitted, even if the local draft is later edited. How should retry behave?

options.text: Generate a new submission ID for each retry and treat each payload as a separate inspection.
Capture the submitted request as an immutable payload and retry that same payload.
Rebuild the request from the latest offline form on every retry.
Capture only the inspection ID and fetch whatever field values are current when retry occurs.
Make the local form permanently immutable before the inspector begins working.

feedback.reason: The prompt says retry means resend the original submitted bytes; rebuilding from an edited form changes the request rather than retrying it.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A retry reuses the submitted immutable payload; an editable form is a separate earlier stage.
details.scenarioApplication: The immutable boundary starts at submission, not while the inspector is still editing the draft.
details.errorCorrection: Rebuilding from the edited form changes the payload; that is a new submission, not a retry of the old one.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The immutable payload begins at submit, not while the local form is still being edited.
details.transfer: A retry should reuse the exact accepted request value; editing creates a new request.

messages.text: The retry would send edited values rather than the accepted request.
An ID alone does not preserve the submitted bytes.
The form remains editable before submission.
A retry repeats one submission; it is not a new submission.

learningObjective: Keep each invoice issue’s timestamp and exact inputs fixed when a corrected issue is created.

question.prompt: In a digital invoice exchange, the billing operator must reissue a rejected invoice. The new issue is traceable and does not double-charge the customer. Every issue records its timestamp and exact address/tax inputs; a corrected reissue creates another retained issue while the customer and sequence continue. How should reissue be stored?

options.text: Make the customer record a new identity for each invoice issue.
Read current address/tax values when rendering an old issue.
Copy the issue shell but retain mutable shared tax inputs from the billing form.
Create a new immutable issue snapshot for the corrected address/tax values and leave the rejected issue intact.
Edit the rejected issue’s address and tax values while keeping its original timestamp.

feedback.reason: The old issue’s timestamp must continue to describe its original inputs; the correction is another issue snapshot.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Each issue snapshot records its own timestamp and exact input values without changing customer continuity.
details.scenarioApplication: The customer/sequence continuity and the per-issue historical values are separate facts; immutable issue values preserve the latter.
details.errorCorrection: Editing the rejected issue while retaining its timestamp makes its recorded inputs false.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The prior issue remains a historical record; reissue values get a separate issue snapshot.
details.transfer: Keep each issued artifact’s timestamp and inputs together when a reissue is a new historical event.

messages.text: That changes the historical inputs while retaining the original issue timestamp.
Customer identity continues across issue records.
Old issues must keep their original input values.
A shared tax object could change the old issue.

learningObjective: Validate related command rules together and publish one immutable set only when no cross-entry conflict remains.

question.prompt: In a smart-building access controller, the facilities administrator must revoke a badge. Revocation is visible to the door policy before access is granted. The published rule set is valid only when no command is both permitted and prohibited; evaluating an isolated entry cannot detect that conflict. What should a policy edit validate and publish?

options.text: Publish each edited rule immediately as the administrator saves it.
Allow the contradictory rules into the active set and resolve their precedence during each access check.
Edit the active collection while the cross-entry validation is still running.
Validate cross-entry conflicts across the full set; publish an immutable replacement only when coherent.
Validate every rule independently, then accept all rows even if two rows contradict each other.

feedback.reason: A command can be both permitted and prohibited only when rules are considered together; validate that whole combination before replacing the active set.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The validity condition is a relation across entries, so one published immutable value must pass the cross-entry check as a complete set.
details.scenarioApplication: The permit/prohibit conflict can span two rows; publishing only individually valid rows does not prove the combined rules are valid.
details.errorCorrection: The nearest alternative is row-by-row validation: it cannot detect the contradictory pair that the prompt makes decisive.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: After a complete set passes, later policy edits create another replacement; this does not freeze policy forever.
details.transfer: When a rule’s validity depends on relationships among entries, validate the combined immutable value before publication.

messages.text: The conflict exists between separate entries, so independent row validation cannot establish that the complete set is coherent.
Incremental publication can expose a partial set and can publish the contradiction before the complete set is checked.
The prompt requires the published set itself to be valid; postponing the conflict moves the invalid state into live decisions.
Readers could observe a mixture of old and new rows before the complete set passes validation.

learningObjective: Apply only the service’s stated normalization rules when constructing a postal value.

question.prompt: In a package-label generation service, the shipping operator must print a label after address correction. The printed label represents the current approved shipment data. For this service, postal values are canonicalized by uppercasing country code and removing spaces from postal code; all other address fields remain significant. A generated label stores that canonical value immutably even if the source form later changes. How should postal values be compared and printed?

options.text: Make each generated label a view over the mutable source form, normalizing its live fields again on every reprint.
Treat each normalized address as an entity with its own generated identity.
Construct an immutable canonical postal value using those stated normalization rules before comparing or printing it.
Compare raw strings, so the two representations the prompt defines as equivalent remain different.
Remove punctuation and accents from every address field even though the prompt defines no such normalization.

feedback.reason: The prompt states exactly which transformations define equivalence; adding more normalization or delaying it would change that contract.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Canonical value construction applies only the equivalence rules explicitly stated for this service.
details.scenarioApplication: The label stores the canonical address produced under the stated country/postal rule; later source-form edits cannot rewrite that generated value.
details.errorCorrection: Normalizing the live source on each later request can change a previously generated label instead of retaining its captured canonical value.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The prompt defines the exact normalization and requires the generated label to retain the result; it does not define extra address-cleaning rules.
details.transfer: Normalize only according to the local equivalence contract, not a general idea of “cleaning” data.

messages.text: That misses equivalence the local contract explicitly defines.
Those extra transformations are not authorized by the stated normalization.
It reads the mutable source again instead of retaining the generated canonical value, so a later edit can rewrite an earlier label.
The prompt describes a value contract, not generated identity.

learningObjective: Review a proposed booking against the exact room and attendee facts captured for that proposal.

question.prompt: In a multi-tenant rehearsal scheduler, the studio coordinator must move a booked rehearsal to a different room. The room capacity and cancellation policy must remain consistent. The move proposal must preserve cancellation policy as well as destination, attendee count, and room capacity. It captures all four at preparation; later edits must not alter that proposal. What should review use?

options.text: Store only the room and reread the live attendee count when an older proposal is reviewed.
Update the confirmed booking’s room before checking the proposal’s captured capacity.
Copy the booking but share mutable attendee data between proposal and confirmed state.
Create a new rehearsal identity for every room proposal.
Review the immutable proposal using captured destination, attendee count, capacity, and cancellation policy.

feedback.reason: Review needs the complete proposed booking facts, including cancellation policy; capturing all four preserves the decision the coordinator evaluates.

details.mechanismOrProperty: The proposal is a value of the facts reviewed together: destination, attendance, capacity, and cancellation policy.
details.scenarioApplication: The captured policy travels with the room and capacity facts, so later policy or attendee edits cannot change what the review approved.
details.errorCorrection: The room-only alternative omits the cancellation policy, one of the conditions the prompt requires the proposal to preserve.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The confirmed booking remains unchanged until the proposal is confirmed; the prompt requires capturing the policy but not freezing future policy versions globally.
details.transfer: When a review depends on a set of facts, make the reviewed proposal contain every fact the reviewer must decide against.

messages.text: The room-only alternative omits cancellation policy, which the prompt requires reviewers to preserve with the other move facts.
Confirmation is a later boundary; changing confirmed state first violates it.
Attendee edits can change what the proposal says was reviewed.
A room proposal does not create a new rehearsal.

learningObjective: Break a mutable caller alias when accepting input into a published immutable collection.

question.prompt: In a museum exhibit controller, the exhibit operator must switch an exhibit into maintenance mode. Unsafe commands are rejected while maintenance is active. The published configuration owns an immutable prohibited-command set. The form supplies a mutable list and may be edited after submission. How should the configuration take ownership of its rules?

options.text: Create a new controller identity for each configuration update.
Copy the mutable form input into an immutable collection at construction so no caller retains a write alias.
Store the form’s mutable list directly and wrap only the configuration getter in a read-only interface.
Deep-copy the entire controller and hardware state whenever one command is added.
Let a command evaluation read the form list directly so it always sees its latest edits.

feedback.reason: Copy the form-owned list into an immutable collection when constructing the published configuration; a read-only getter alone would not sever the form’s mutable alias.

details.mechanismOrProperty: Copying into an immutable collection at the ownership boundary prevents an input alias from mutating published configuration.
details.scenarioApplication: The form still holds the mutable list after publication, so the published configuration must own an immutable copy rather than a wrapper over the form’s collection.
details.errorCorrection: A read-only wrapper does not break the form’s alias to the same mutable list.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The published rule set is immutable; a future edit constructs another value rather than freezing the controller forever.
details.transfer: Break mutable aliases when accepting input into a published immutable collection.

messages.text: The form still owns and can mutate the shared list reference.
Copying controller hardware state does not solve the list alias.
The published configuration should not follow unsubmitted form edits.
A configuration edit does not change controller identity.

learningObjective: Return a new immutable progress-set value so a later completion does not mutate a snapshot already held by report readers.

question.prompt: In a video-learning library, the curriculum editor retires a lesson while preserving learner progress. A profile exposes its completed lesson IDs as an immutable snapshot; report readers may retain the loaded snapshot while a later completion is added. What should the progress update return?

options.text: Wrap a mutable shared list in a read-only view and append the completion through the profile editor.
Rebuild progress from currently active catalog lessons, dropping retired lesson IDs.
Assign a new lesson identity for the completion so the old set does not need updating.
Return a new immutable progress set with the completed lesson ID; retain the old snapshot for readers already using it.
Mutate the existing set so every reader of the old snapshot sees the new completion.

feedback.reason: A new immutable set can represent the updated profile while report readers keep the earlier snapshot they loaded.

details.mechanismOrProperty: An immutable collection update returns a new value; readers holding the prior value continue to see that prior set.
details.scenarioApplication: The profile can advance with one added lesson ID while an already loaded report continues to use its unchanged snapshot.
details.errorCorrection: Mutating the old set changes the snapshot that report readers already retained.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Only the progress collection value is replaced; retired lesson identity remains present for existing progress.
details.transfer: When immutable snapshots are shared with readers, represent an update as a new collection value rather than mutating the old snapshot.

messages.text: Mutating the old set changes the snapshot that report readers already retained.
A read-only view still shares a mutable backing list, so the editor can change the supposedly fixed snapshot.
Retiring a lesson must not delete its ID from learner progress.
Completing a lesson records progress against its existing identity; it does not create another lesson.

learningObjective: Capture all fields needed for a coherent export from one board revision.

question.prompt: In a shared whiteboard application, the session host must close a board and export its history. Export observes a stable session state. Editing continues during export; strokes and participant labels must both come from the same board revision. What should the export builder read?

options.text: Capture strokes and labels together into one immutable export input before rendering.
Copy strokes at the start but resolve participant labels from the live board later.
Pause all editing permanently when the first export starts.
Have the renderer query each live field as it needs it.
Create a new board identity for each export.

feedback.reason: Mixing a captured stroke list with later live labels can create an export that never existed as one board revision.

details.mechanismOrProperty: One export input snapshot must contain all fields whose consistency is required.
details.scenarioApplication: Capture only the fields needed for a coherent export; the board can remain editable after that snapshot.
details.errorCorrection: Later live labels can be paired with earlier strokes, yielding a board view from no single revision.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: Editing can continue after capture; the export builder reads the fixed snapshot.
details.transfer: Capture every field needed for one coherent output at the same snapshot boundary.

messages.text: Those fields can come from different revisions.
The prompt allows editing to continue.
Live reads do not provide the required same-revision guarantee.
Exporting does not create a new board.

learningObjective: Keep transfer-time owner and deadline facts fixed while the support case continues to change.

question.prompt: In a customer-support escalation desk, the support lead must escalate a conversation. The escalation keeps ownership and response deadlines. The transfer receipt records owner and deadline at transfer; the support case’s live owner and deadline may later change. What should the receipt represent?

options.text: Keep a read-only receipt view backed by the case’s mutable owner/deadline fields.
Change the conversation identity whenever it moves to another support owner.
Store an immutable transfer value with the owner and deadline effective at the transfer.
Render old transfer receipts from the case’s current owner and deadline.
Make the whole support case immutable after its first transfer.

feedback.reason: The live case may change, but the receipt must still describe the specific transfer event and its deadline.

details.mechanismOrProperty: A transfer receipt is a historical value; the support case remains the changing entity.
details.scenarioApplication: Freeze the transfer facts in the receipt without freezing the ongoing support case.
details.errorCorrection: A receipt that follows current case fields stops describing its own transfer.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The receipt is immutable while the support case continues its live lifecycle.
details.transfer: Keep historical transfer facts separate from the case’s current mutable fields.

messages.text: That changes the receipt after the transfer it records.
The case continues to change after transfer.
A read-only wrapper over live fields remains live.
The case identity continues across transfers.
